title: Nothing checks formatting: the gate is go test, which does not care
description:
The declared gate is 'go test -short -count=1 -timeout 45m -parallel 12 ./...'. go test does not check gofmt, so an unformatted file can merge and stay merged indefinitely. internal/reconcile/restart_test.go was unformatted from the moment it merged until the usx worker found it at its base and filed it (repaired as 1d5a8f2).

A worker finding it is the system working, but it should not need a worker: the check is one command and it is deterministic, which is exactly the kind of thing a gate should carry rather than a person or an agent noticing.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the repository wants more than gofmt - go vet already runs as part of go test, but staticcheck/golangci-lint do not - and whether a formatting failure should refuse a tick the way a test failure does, or be reported separately. A formatting violation is not a claim about behaviour, so refusing a tick for it may be the wrong shape.
acceptance_criteria: An unformatted file cannot reach the integration branch unnoticed: the repository declares a formatting check and it runs where the gate runs. The check names the files and is fast enough that it does not add meaningfully to the gate. A deliberately unformatted file fails it.
